reason: Entire is the standard margin state of a leaf blade. The examples are correct.
'Leaf entire' means the blade margin is entire. This is a normal flora shorthand, and the examples fit.
The colour of the upper leaf surface is meaningful. 'Glaucous adaxially' is a colour/surface state that fits here.
The colour of the lower leaf surface is meaningful. A statement such as 'glabrous with silvery scales beneath' also has other qualities and should be split.
'3-nerved' is the number of veins of the lamina, a count.
'Glands present/absent' is a presence statement about secretory structures. It is only meaningful when the gland is the entity, and the examples show that.

'characteristic' is the root PATO term and is too generic to be a quality. The examples are alternatives such as 'entire or undulate' or 'glabrous or ciliate', which belong to specific qualities of the margin.
A ciliate margin is a common leaf trait. The bearer is the margin, but the lamina is acceptable.
An entire leaf margin is the core use of this term.
A revolute margin is a leaf trait. The margin is part of the lamina, and negations ('not revolute') are handled elsewhere.
Stigma lobe count from '3-lobed' is a counted part, and flora_counted_parts maps lobed to lobe.
The colour of the corolla lip is meaningful.
An entire sepal margin is meaningful. 'Outer tepals entire' is also acceptable.
An entire bract margin is meaningful. The appendages example is a weaker case but harmless.
'Veins obscure' means inconspicuous veins, and a vascular bundle is the vein entity used here.
A decurrent lamina base running down the petiole or stem is a standard leaf trait.
The root term 'characteristic' is too generic. 'Simple or branched' belongs to a branching quality, not here.
This is a count of labellum lobes from '3-lobed'. The apex of the labellum in some examples is a minor imprecision.
This is a count of teeth on the leaf blade.
Papillate, scabrellous and similar surface textures of phyllaries are meaningful. 'Callous' is a wrong reading, but the rest is correct.
A winged fruit is a standard trait.
Tapering base or blade is a standard leaf trait.
A stout pedicel is a thick pedicel. The synonym 'stout' fits PATO.
The root term 'characteristic' is too generic. The examples (arching, erect, channeled, entire or denticulate) belong to specific qualities.
An entire leaflet margin is meaningful.
An entire petal margin is meaningful.
'Rooting at nodes' means shoot-borne roots are present or absent. This is meaningful, and the negation is handled.
A crenate margin fits PATO scalloped (synonym crenate).
The shape of a corolla lobe is meaningful.
A hairy pedicel is meaningful.
The number of nodes of a stem is a count.
'Pairs of pinnules' counts pinnules, which is correct, but 'sori 1-4 per pinnule' counts sori and the pinnule is only the container. A rule would need to tell a counted part from a 'per X' container.
The length of a perigynium is meaningful. Only 5 floras, but a normal Carex trait.
A glandular pedicel is meaningful.
'3-fid' is the number of style branches, and flora_counted_parts maps fid to lobe.
The width of a perigynium is meaningful. Wing width is a wing quality, though, and a rule should keep it apart.
The length of an orchid column (gynostemium) is meaningful.
A herbaceous leaf blade is a texture/consistency state used in floras.
The colour of an indusium is meaningful.
The number of pyrenes in a drupe is a counted part.
The number of cauline leaves is a count.
The shape of an involucral bract (phyllary) is meaningful.
The colour of a perigynium is meaningful. The beak colour examples belong to the beak, but the pair itself is fine.
Papillose texture of a moss peristome tooth is a standard bryophyte trait.
The length of an orchid labellum is meaningful.
The colour of a spathe is meaningful. 'Tube green' belongs to the tube, so check it in a rule.
The number of vittae (oil tubes) is a count.
An undulate (wavy) margin is a standard leaf trait.
The length of a moss operculum is meaningful.
Wrong reading. 'Oblique' for a sepal means asymmetric or slanted in shape, but PATO 'oblique orientation' is the angle of a part to an axis.
Wrong reading. 'Withering' is the dying process of the leaf, while PATO 'shriveled' is a dried, wrinkled state, so the pair would be a doubtful match.
A triangular lobe is a shape of the lobe. Deltate fits the same term.
A subglobose ovary is a spheroid shape.
'Petiolulate' means a petiolule is present. This is a normal presence statement.
An acute apex of a corolla lobe is a meaningful sharpness state. The apex is the lobe's part, which is acceptable.
A cylindrical capsule is a meaningful fruit shape.
A flat (plane) leaf margin is meaningful and opposes revolute or undulate.
An oblong involucral bract is a meaningful shape.
An oblong corolla lobe is a meaningful shape.
Wrong reading. An oblique leaf base means unequal sides (asymmetric), not an orientation, which PATO oblique orientation describes.
